decisions.reason: Grounds diagnosis in agent-session-log.txt quoted lines (npm cleaning/remove 16:41:02-16:41:05, linkStuff) and env-state.txt; explicitly connects the tool worker as a child of the host process being replaced, explains the host died mid-install so the tool result could never be durably recorded, preserves the unknown outcome, and treats it as structural self-host dependency failure rather than a network flake without overclaiming a universal crash rule.

Reads env-state.txt precisely: rc.1 package content present while dsh/dsh.cmd are missing and dsh.ps1 is stale; explains npm generates bin shims at the end of install so content presence does not imply a complete install; notes the user's hand-swap made it non-standard and rejects hand-copying directories or hand-writing shims as repair.

Grounds the remedy in repair-notes.md: re-run the pinned `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-rc.1` from an external tool outside the stopped host so npm regenerates the shims; verify `dsh --version` equals rc.1; covers checkout alignment to dsh-v0.1.2-rc.1 with no unrelated source edits; clearly separates the recorded external repair from what the candidate itself did (read-only).

Explicitly states the agent runs inside the upgrade target and must hand off rather than execute the global install in-session; prescribes fully stopping all dsh processes first (browser refresh is not a stop), exact-version pinning (bare install can resolve to latest), then restart/hard-refresh/verify from an external terminal (not a dsh tool call, so no dependent-shell ambiguity); distinguishes stop-first and pinning as established rules and the in-session refusal plus interrupted-recovery as incident-specific additions.

Proposes a concrete guard comparing the install target against the running process's own module origin plus a recovery rule for the shim-less signature; uses repair-notes.md's 252-file version-only alpha.5→rc.1 diff to conclude no plugin re-migration and no code changes; checklist covers version markers, shim consistency, restart/hard-refresh and actual plugin loading, and optional dsh-old-* backup cleanup only after rc.1 is confirmed.

caps.reason: The report's final advice consistently refuses in-session execution ('must never execute the global install itself', 'refuse and respond with the external hand-off procedure'); in-session execution appears only as the analyzed past failure and rejected bad example.

The final fix is the formal external pinned re-install; hand directory swaps and hand-written shims appear only as described/rejected bad examples ('never hand-copy package directories or hand-write shims').
